 4         1.     This class action arises out of the recent data security incident and
 5   data breach that was perpetrated against Defendant Serviceaide (the “Data
 6   Breach”), which held in its possession certain personally identifiable information
 7   (“PII”) and protected health information (“PHI”) (collectively, “the Private
 8   Information”) of Plaintiff and other individuals associated i.e., the putative Class
 9   Members (“Class”), who are patients of Catholic Health, which is a customer of
10   Defendant Serviceaide. This Data Breach occurred between about September 19,
11   2024, and November 5, 2024.
12         2.     Following its internal investigation, Defendant learned that the data of
13   at least one of Defendant’s clients, Catholic Health System, Inc’s (“Catholic
14   Health”), was compromised in the Data Breach including certain personal or
15   protected health information of approximately 500,000 individuals.
16         3.     The exposed data included, but was not limited to: full names, dates of
17   birth, Social Security numbers (“personally identifying information” or “PII”), and
18   medical record numbers, patient account numbers, medical/health information,
19   health insurance information, treatment information, prescriptions, clinical
20   information, provider names and locations, and email/usernames and passwords
21   (“protected health information” or “PHI”; collectively with PII, Private
22   Information).
23         4.     According to its Breach Notice, on November 15, 2024, Serviceaide
24   learned that “certain information within its Catholic Health Elasticsearch database
25   was inadvertently made publicly available.” Following an internal investigation,
26   Defendant determined that between September 19, 2024 and November 5, 2024,
27   certain highly sensitive Catholic Health patient information was made publicly
28   available.

 1         5.     Although Defendant asserts that it has no evidence that information

 3         6.     In other words, Defendant’s cyber and data security systems were so

 5   Private Information to be publicly available for 47 days. The Data Breach was a

14   that their information had been subject to the unauthorized access and exfiltration.

17   computer network in a condition vulnerable to public exposure, exfiltration, and
18   cyberattacks.

20   potential for improper disclosure of Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ Private

27   unauthorized intrusions; failing to disclose that it did not have adequately robust
28   computer systems and security practices to safeguard Plaintiff’s and Class

 1   Members’ Private Information; failing to take standard and reasonably available

 5   computer network and systems that housed the Private Information. Had
 6   Serviceaide properly monitored its property, it would have discovered the intrusion

25   financial accounts to guard against identity theft.

27   costs for, e.g., purchasing credit monitoring services, credit freezes, credit reports,
28   or other protective measures to deter and detect identity theft.
